claims.text: Phase evolution in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs can be reproducibly controlled by precisely tuning annealing temperature and cooling rate.
An integrated dynamic in situ measurement method can monitor phase transitions in real time.
Real-time in situ monitoring enables reproducible control of phase evolution.
Conventional processing of Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs yields a mixture of phases with uncontrolled distributions.
Phase evolution can be steered by applying controlled annealing temperatures and cooling rates while monitoring the microstructure in situ.
High-temperature DSC combined with synchrotron XRD can provide the proposed real-time phase measurements under non-equilibrium annealing conditions.
The formation, transformation, and ordering of constituent phases can be observed through real-time XRD patterns.
The degree of chemical or phase ordering affects mechanical behavior in HEAs.
Changing annealing temperature changes thermodynamic parameters relevant to phase stability and transformation.
Changing cooling rate changes kinetic parameters that drive phase transformations in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs.
Real-time measurement feedback permits fine tuning of thermal parameters to steer phase evolution toward desired microstructures.
The proposed method will make phase evolution more predictable and reproducible than conventional processing.
Controlling phase or chemical ordering can improve mechanical properties.
The proposed method can produce controlled lamellar or eutectic phase distributions.
Standard melting and rolling approaches rely on empirical changes and lack real-time phase feedback.
The resolution of in situ measurement techniques may limit the effectiveness of the proposed control method.
Coupled thermodynamic and kinetic effects under non-equilibrium conditions may limit control of phase evolution.
The quantitative effects of the integrated in situ approach on phase fractions and transformation kinetics have not been established.
